support_bodies.name: lead-notch and west service-furniture tree
support_bodies.rationale: The ASSE pan sleeve's flat lead-notch roof is the first contact. It shares the support body required by the west-wall service and ceiling-strip contacts above it, adding one interface island without adding a connected support body. The combined tree grows from the bed through the open enclosure.

support_bodies.name: forward west service-furniture tree
support_bodies.rationale: The west-wall service contacts in this forward depth band keep the routing, anchor and seam-clearance lanes open. Their seven interfaces share one bed-rooted tree instead of separate stacks rooted on the wall furniture.

support_bodies.name: middle west service-furniture tree
support_bodies.rationale: The west-wall service contacts in this depth band keep the component and wiring lanes open. Their four interfaces share one bed-rooted tree instead of separate stacks rooted on the wall furniture.

support_bodies.name: core-holds, pan sleeve and rear-wall service tree
support_bodies.rationale: The first two contacts carry the cold core's aft hold-down soffits over its insertion lane. The ASSE pan sleeve's remaining floor and the rear-wall service contacts above them join the same removable body. A pillar in the core lane blocks insertion, and the retained tree grows from the bed through the open enclosure.

support_bodies.name: east Wago-roof and ceiling-strip tree
support_bodies.rationale: Each of the five Wago wells keeps one complete flat ceiling that grips its lever nut. Those five contacts and the two +X ceiling-strip contacts form one bed-rooted tree instead of short stacks on the wall furniture or seam.

support_bodies.name: collet-plate stop and pump-bay lintel tree
support_bodies.rationale: The lower contact carries the exact 1 mm flat land that stops the steel collet plate and defines its Z datum; its fore edge is already raked at 45 degrees. The upper contact is the lintel that closes the full-width removable pump-cartridge bay while carrying the display above it. A support-free gable across that deep opening would occupy the rectangular cartridge-withdrawal or display envelope. The two contacts share one long bed-rooted tree, so neither hides a separate short or material-rooted support.

support_bodies.name: X- pump boss-bearing shoulder
support_bodies.rationale: The flat annular shoulder bears axially on the fitted pump boss while the complete octagonal wall locates X, Y and yaw. Chamfering the shoulder would trade away bearing area rather than remove an accidental overhang; its centre bore remains open for direct support removal.
